questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.learningObjective: Define the mole as a counting unit
questions.stem: A city planner's memo asks what a mole counts; which answer is correct?

options.text: Exactly one gram of any substance.
Exactly one liter of gas at STP.

questions.explanation: A mole is Avogadro's number of particles. Gram, liter, and single atom are different quantities.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: Why is the mole useful as a counting unit in chemistry?

answer.exemplar: The mole groups Avogadro's number of particles so chemists can count by weighing, bridging microscopic particles and macroscopic mass.

questions.explanation: It connects particle counts to measurable mass. Counting individual particles is impractical.

questions.subject: CHEMISTRY
questions.stem: Is a mole a unit of mass, volume, or count?

answer.exemplar: A mole is a unit of count (amount of substance), not mass or volume, though it can be converted to either using molar mass or molar volume.

questions.explanation: It counts particles; mass and volume are derived via molar mass or molar volume.
